presentingComplaint: 3 months of palpitations, unintentional weight loss and heat intolerance
history: A 32-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of intermittent palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance, excessive sweating and a 6 kg unintentional weight loss despite an increased appetite. She reports anxiety, irritability, poor sleep and increasingly frequent, looser bowel motions. Menstrual periods have become lighter and infrequent (oligomenorrhoea). She has noticed mild bilateral eye grittiness and a sense of staring. No prior thyroid disease; mother has autoimmune hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's). No amiodarone, iodinated contrast, thyroid hormone or excess iodine intake. Non-smoker. No neck pain, fever or recent viral illness.
examination: Anxious, fidgety young woman with warm, moist palms and a fine resting tremor of the outstretched hands. Diffuse, smooth, non-tender goitre with an audible bruit over the gland. Regular tachycardia; no murmur or signs of heart failure. Mild bilateral proptosis with lid retraction and lid lag; conjunctivae mildly injected, no chemosis or ophthalmoplegia. Brisk reflexes. Pretibial skin normal. Pertinent negatives: no fever, no neck tenderness, GCS 15, no delirium, no high-output cardiac failure, no atrial fibrillation on this visit - i.e. no features of thyroid storm (Burch-Wartofsky low).

labs.Full blood count: normal; mild normocytic anaemia Hb 11.9 g/dL

imaging: Thyroid ultrasound: diffusely enlarged, hypervascular gland ('thyroid inferno' on colour Doppler), no discrete nodule. Radioactive iodine uptake (if antibody equivocal) would show diffuse increased uptake - not required here as TRAb is positive.
citations: Harrison 22e - Hyperthyroidism and Thyrotoxicosis (Disorders of the Thyroid Gland)
ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis 2016
contraindications: Propylthiouracil preferred over carbimazole/methimazole only in first trimester of pregnancy (carbimazole embryopathy risk); confirm not pregnant before radioiodine
Beta-blocker (propranolol) contraindicated/cautioned in asthma - use rate-limiting alternative if reactive airway disease
Radioactive iodine contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding and active moderate-severe Graves' orbitopathy
edgeCases: Apathetic thyrotoxicosis in the elderly may present with weight loss, atrial fibrillation and depression rather than classic adrenergic features
Thyroiditis (subacute or post-partum) causes thyrotoxicosis with LOW radioiodine uptake and negative TRAb - do not treat with antithyroid drugs
Untreated thyrotoxicosis with an intercurrent stressor can decompensate into thyroid storm (Burch-Wartofsky >45)
expectedMaiK: Suppressed TSH with elevated free T4/T3, a positive TSH-receptor antibody, diffuse goitre with bruit and orbitopathy in a young woman is diagnostic of Graves' thyrotoxicosis. Manage with an antithyroid drug (carbimazole/methimazole) plus a beta-blocker for symptom control, and confirm pregnancy status before considering radioiodine.
expectedNextQuestions: Any pregnancy or plan of pregnancy, and last menstrual period?
Any amiodarone, iodinated contrast, kelp/iodine supplements or exogenous thyroid hormone?
Any eye symptoms (pain, diplopia, visual loss) suggesting active orbitopathy?
expectedInvestigations: Thyroid ultrasound with colour Doppler (or radioiodine uptake scan if aetiology unclear)

investigations: Free T4 / free T3 with suppressed TSH

regressionAssertions: must not classify as infective / must not recommend antibiotics
thyroid_storm must NOT be top-1 given absent fever, normal sensorium and low Burch-Wartofsky
